verses.context: Each verse of 169-176 begins with taw, the twenty-second and last Hebrew letter. The psalm ends not with triumph but with prayer, praise and humility. Psalm 102:1 prays, 'Let my cry for help come before You.'
explore: A loud call for help, an earnest plea lifted up to God.
Insight and discernment that come from God's own teaching.
verses.reflect: What do you still want to understand about God, and will you ask Him?
verses.alt: The last rays of evening sun falling on an open scroll.

verses.title: My plea before You
verses.heading: Rescue me according to Your promise
verses.meaning: 'May my plea come before You; rescue me according to Your promise.' He brings his request for mercy before God's throne. He asks for deliverance, resting not on his record but on God's promise. To the very end, his hope rests on what God has said. His final pleas rest on the same promises that carried him through the whole psalm.
verses.context: The word 'plea' means a request for grace or favor. 1 Kings 8:28-30 records Solomon asking God to hear the pleas of His people. Hebrews 4:16 invites approaching God's throne of grace with confidence.
explore: A humble request for mercy or favor from someone in authority.
Snatch someone away from danger and deliver them to safety.
verses.reflect: What plea do you want to bring before God today, trusting His promise?
verses.alt: A doorway open into a quiet courtyard of an old temple with no people.

verses.title: Lips pour forth praise
verses.heading: You teach me Your statutes
verses.meaning: 'My lips pour forth praise, for You teach me Your statutes.' Praise overflows like water bubbling from a spring. The reason is surprising: because God teaches him. Being taught by God is itself a cause for joy. Learning God's ways makes the heart sing. Praise is the natural overflow of a heart God has taught.
verses.context: The verb means to bubble up or gush forth. Psalm 19:2 says day to day pours forth speech. Psalm 45:1 says, 'My heart overflows with a pleasing theme.'
explore: Bubble up and overflow like water from a spring that cannot be contained.
Words of honor and thanks offered to God for His goodness.
verses.reflect: What has God taught you lately that makes you want to praise Him?
verses.alt: A spring bubbling over smooth stones in a sunny clearing.

verses.title: Tongue that sings
verses.heading: All Your commandments are righteous
verses.meaning: 'My tongue sings of Your word, for all Your commandments are righteous.' His tongue answers God's word with song. He sings because God's commands are all right and good. Worship and Scripture belong together. The word we learn becomes the song we sing. Song is a way to remember and to celebrate what God has spoken.
verses.context: Many hymns and songs are drawn from Scripture. Ephesians 5:19 encourages speaking to one another in psalms, hymns and spiritual songs. Exodus 15 records Israel's song after God's deliverance.
explore: Speech itself, the instrument of speaking and singing aloud.
Right, just and good, in full agreement with God's own character.
verses.reflect: Is there a Bible verse you could turn into a song or prayer this week?
verses.alt: A small group of villagers singing together in an evening courtyard.

verses.title: A ready hand
verses.heading: May Your hand be ready to help me
verses.meaning: 'May Your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen Your precepts.' God's hand stands for His power to act. The psalmist asks that it be ready, close and near to help. He has chosen God's way, and now he asks God to help the one who has chosen Him. Choosing God's ways leads to trusting God's help. He leans on God's hand.
verses.context: God's hand is a common image of His power (Exodus 13:3; Isaiah 59:1). Isaiah 41:10 says, 'I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.' God's hand is pictured both as strong to save and gentle to uphold.
explore: A symbol in Scripture of power, protection and practical help.
Deliberately selected and committed to after weighing the options.
verses.reflect: Where do you need God's ready help today, and how could you ask for it?
verses.alt: A sturdy wooden handrail along a steep stone stairway.

verses.title: Longing and delight
verses.heading: I long for Your salvation
verses.meaning: 'I long for Your salvation, O LORD, and Your law is my delight.' Near the end, he sums up his heart in two phrases. He longs for God's rescue, still waiting. And he delights in God's law, already enjoying it. Longing and delight live together in the heart of a believer. Waiting and enjoying are both part of walking with God.
verses.context: Believers both enjoy God's gifts now and long for full salvation. Romans 8:23 says we groan inwardly as we wait eagerly. Psalm 1:2 describes delight in the law of the LORD.
explore: Yearn and desire deeply for something not yet fully received.
Joy and pleasure in something that satisfies the heart.
verses.reflect: What do you already enjoy from God, and what are you still longing for?
verses.alt: A traveler resting by a cool stream, gazing toward distant mountains.

verses.title: Live to praise
verses.heading: Let me live to praise You
verses.meaning: 'Let me live to praise You; may Your judgments sustain me.' He asks for life, and he says what he will do with it: praise God. Life's purpose is worship. And he asks God's rulings to help and support him along the way. God's word both guides life and holds it up. Life and praise are tied together from the first verse of the psalm to the last.
verses.context: Isaiah 38:19 says, 'The living, the living, they thank You.' Psalm 146:2 says, 'I will praise the LORD all my life.' 1 Peter 2:9 says we are called to declare His praises.
explore: Have life and continue living, with breath to praise God.
Help, support and hold up someone who would otherwise fall.
verses.reflect: How could your life today be an act of praise to God in word and deed?
verses.alt: A village at sunrise with smoke rising from morning fires and birds overhead.

verses.title: Seek Your lost sheep
verses.heading: I have strayed like a lost sheep
verses.meaning: 'I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek Your servant, for I have not forgotten Your commandments.' The longest psalm ends with humility. After all his love and obedience, the psalmist confesses he still wanders. He does not say he will find his own way home. He asks the Shepherd to seek him. The whole psalm ends in grace.
verses.context: Isaiah 53:6 says, 'We all like sheep have gone astray.' Jesus told of the shepherd leaving ninety-nine sheep to find one lost (Luke 15:4-7) and said He came to seek and save the lost (Luke 19:10).
explore: Wandered off and gone astray, away from the shepherd and the flock.
Search for and go looking for someone until they are found.
verses.reflect: Where have you wandered, and will you let the Shepherd find you?
verses.alt: A shepherd searching rocky hills at dusk for a single lost sheep.
